principles.statement: Strip-based serpentine construction with 2-opt local search and carrot-aware prime placement scores ~55.45 on Frontier-CS problem 44, near the top of the 45-60 predicted range, demonstrating that geometric tour optimization combined with penalty avoidance is effective for this TSP variant.
principles.regime: Frontier-CS problem 44 (Traveling Santa with Carrot Constraint), N up to 200K, 2.5s time limit, 20 test cases
principles.mechanism: Strip construction groups cities into horizontal bands (sqrt(N*H/W) strips) and visits them in serpentine order, reducing expected step distance from ~H/3 (x-sorted baseline) to ~max(W,H)/sqrt(N). 2-opt with adaptive window (30 for large N, up to N for small N) eliminates crossing edges, running until 2.1s. Carrot optimization swaps prime-numbered cities to penalty positions (indices 9, 19, 29, ...) to avoid the 10% penalty multiplier on those steps.
principles.applicability_bounds: Holds for the current test data mix (20 test cases, N from 10 to 200K). Score of 55.45 leaves room for improvement — theoretical maximum is 100 but practically limited by the scoring curve (s_full = N^0.6, tau=1.25). 2-opt window sizes are time-constrained.

principles.statement: The 2-opt local optimum for strip-based tours is robust within window-based search, but spatial NN-list 2-opt escapes this local optimum by checking geometrically nearby cities regardless of tour order. NN-list 2-opt with K=20 achieves 76.3 (from NN construction) vs 55.4 for window-based 2-opt, confirming that the iter-1 ceiling was a search limitation, not a true local optimum.
principles.regime: Frontier-CS problem 44, N up to 200K, 2.5s time limit
principles.mechanism: Window-based 2-opt checks edges within a fixed tour-order window (25-300 depending on N). For N=200K with window=25, this only checks 0.01% of possible edge pairs. Spatial NN-list 2-opt checks edges involving the K=20 nearest spatial neighbors of each city, finding improving swaps between geometrically close cities that are far apart in tour order. This is a fundamentally different search strategy that explores a much larger neighborhood in the same time.
principles.applicability_bounds: The 76.3 score may itself be a local optimum of the NN-list 2-opt. 3-opt or Lin-Kernighan style moves could potentially escape it. Also, the K=20 NN list may miss beneficial swaps with cities beyond the 20th nearest neighbor.

principles.statement: The carrot constraint (10% penalty on every 10th step) contributes only ~1-5% of total penalized cost. Geometric tour optimization dominates score improvement.
principles.mechanism: Approximately N/10 steps are penalty positions. Even if all are penalized, the 10% surcharge on N/10 steps adds only 1% to total cost. After geometric optimization reduces edge lengths, the absolute penalty savings from carrot swaps are small. Not directly measured via ablation in iter-1.
principles.applicability_bounds: Estimated from the penalty structure; iter-2 should test geometry-only vs carrot-only to confirm quantitatively.

principles.statement: NN construction + spatial NN-list 2-opt (K=20) scores 76.3 on Frontier-CS problem 44, a 20.9-point improvement over strip + window 2-opt (55.4). The spatial NN-list is the dominant improvement (~11 points), with NN construction adding ~10 points over strip construction. The algorithm converges deterministically within the 2.5s time budget.
principles.regime: Frontier-CS problem 44, N up to 200K, 2.5s time limit, 20 test cases
principles.mechanism: Spatial NN-list 2-opt precomputes K=20 nearest neighbors per city using dual x-sorted and y-sorted windows, then uses these as candidate edges for 2-opt swaps. This finds cross-tour improvements that window-based 2-opt misses (window=25-30 for N=200K only checks tour-order neighbors). NN construction produces a locally-connected initial tour that is close to the 2-opt local optimum, enabling deterministic convergence within the time budget. Strip construction produces a tour with long inter-strip edges that requires more 2-opt iterations to fix.
principles.applicability_bounds: Tested with K=20, W_nn=40-150 depending on N. Higher K may help marginally but precompute cost scales linearly. The 76.3 score leaves room for improvement — approaches like 3-opt, Lin-Kernighan moves, or multi-start NN construction could push higher.

principles.statement: NN construction provides both quality and stability advantages over strip construction: the 2-opt-converged tour is ~10 points better (76.3 vs 66.2 mean), and convergence is deterministic (std=0.0 vs std=3.8). The construction heuristic determines not just initial tour quality but also whether 2-opt can converge within the time budget.
principles.regime: Frontier-CS problem 44, spatial NN-list 2-opt with K=20, 2.5s time limit
principles.mechanism: NN construction from city 0 greedily visits the nearest unvisited neighbor, producing a tour where consecutive cities are spatially close. This tour has fewer crossing edges and shorter inter-step distances, so the NN-list 2-opt converges before the time limit. Strip construction sorts cities by y into horizontal bands and traverses them serpentine-style, creating long inter-strip edges. These require more 2-opt passes to eliminate, and the time budget runs out before full convergence on large test cases (N=100K-200K), explaining the high score variance.
principles.applicability_bounds: The stability advantage is specific to time-budgeted optimization. With unlimited time, both construction methods would converge to the same 2-opt local optimum. The ~10 point quality gap may shrink with more time or larger NN 2-opt windows.

principles.statement: Multi-start NN construction, or-opt (single-city relocation), and 2-opt cycling detection are all individually neutral for this problem at the 2-opt-converged tour quality level. Multi-start finds equivalent-quality local optima (different starts converge to same tour cost). Or-opt finds no improving moves after 2-opt convergence. Cycling detection saves time on grid test cases but does not improve tour quality. The combination has no synergy — all three are neutral, producing sum-of-zero improvement.
principles.regime: NN construction + NN-list 2-opt (K=20) on Frontier-CS problem 44 test cases (N=10 to 200000)
principles.mechanism: Multi-start NN explores different starting cities but all 2-opt-converged tours reach the same local optimum quality (within ±0.3% per test case). Or-opt's single-city relocation neighborhood is subsumed by 2-opt — any or-opt-improving move would also be detected by 2-opt (removing a city and reinserting it is equivalent to two 2-opt moves). Cycling detection correctly identifies 2-opt cycles on grid data (exact same number of improvements per pass) and breaks them, saving ~1500ms on TC6 (N=15000 grid 2501×6), but the freed time is insufficient for meaningful additional optimization.
principles.applicability_bounds: Applies to NN+2-opt framework with K=20 NN-list. Does NOT apply to fundamentally different neighborhoods (3-opt, LK moves, which can escape 2-opt local optima). Does NOT apply to different construction heuristics that might produce tours with different 2-opt basins.

principles.statement: The 2-opt local optimum is a hard ceiling for score improvement on this problem. Multi-start, ILS (double-bridge perturbation), or-opt, and cycling detection all converge to the same ~76.3 score. Breaking through requires 3-opt, Lin-Kernighan moves, or problem-specific construction heuristics that exploit data structure (e.g., correlated coordinates in TC4/TC7).
principles.mechanism: The 2-opt-optimal tour has uniform basin quality across different constructions (NN from city 0, NN from random cities, strip construction + 2-opt). Or-opt and ILS cannot escape these basins because their perturbation magnitudes are insufficient — or-opt relocates single cities (too fine-grained), and ILS double-bridge produces tours that 2-opt reconverges to the same quality. Only moves that simultaneously change 3+ edges (3-opt, LK) can escape 2-opt-local-optimal basins.
principles.applicability_bounds: Specific to Frontier-CS problem 44 data distributions. Different TSP instances with different spatial structure might have different 2-opt basin characteristics.
